_note: Declared divergences between an authoritative source and the value the shipped code actually uses. A deviation is RECORDED, never silently 'fixed': gate-deviations anchors mechanical values with a file+regex+value triple, so changing the code without changing this ledger fails the gate and changing the ledger without changing the code fails it too. An OPEN deviation must name the week that closes it. A deviation whose source is a judgement rather than a number declares sourceUnit 'n/a' and is exempt from anchoring — a regex cannot capture 'the boundary condition table is the wrong table' — but it is still held to the full schema, so it cannot be quietly deleted.

deviations.description: Three values for concrete unit weight. IRC:6-2017 Cl. 204.1 Table 1 gives 24 kN/m³ for plain concrete and 25 kN/m³ for reinforced concrete. loadCalc.ts uses 24 (plain); slabCalc.ts hardcodes 25 (RC); coefficients.json says 25. The deliverable slab engine (bridge-excel-generator/design-engine.ts) uses 24. All three are defensible — the deviation is that the choice is not explicit anywhere.
deviations.notes: Do NOT silently patch. Record the engineering decision here and in the re-accepted verify:engine snapshot. Until decided, all three values remain in force in their respective modules.

deviations.quantity: asphalt / bituminous wearing coat unit weight
deviations.description: coefficients.json records 24 kN/m³ for asphalt; loadCalc.ts DEFAULT_DEAD_LOAD uses 22 kN/m³. IRC:6-2017 Cl. 204.1 Table 1 gives 22 kN/m³ for bituminous concrete, 24 kN/m³ for stone masonry. The code value (22) matches IRC for bituminous wearing coat. The coefficients.json value (24) may be a copy-paste from stone masonry.
deviations.notes: Do NOT silently patch. Needs engineer review.

deviations.description: A cantilever slab is a one-way slab (IS 456:2000 Cl. 24.1). slabCalc.ts routes 'cantilever' to 'four_edges_disc' in the two-way Table 26 lookup, which is the wrong table and produces wrong moment coefficients. The one-way branch handles cantilever correctly (suppCoeff = 0.5). The two-way branch is only reached if the user explicitly sets slabType='twoway' AND boundaryCondition='cantilever', which is a contradiction.
deviations.decidedValue: warn when slabType=twoway AND bc=cantilever; treat as one-way
deviations.notes: The warning is already emitted by slabInputSchema. The bcToKey mapping remains as-is until W03 adds a validation that rejects slabType=twoway+bc=cantilever as an invalid combination.

deviations.quantity: calcAst() silent return for doubly-reinforced section
deviations.sourceValue: fail-loud: discriminant < 0 means the section is under-sized
deviations.description: When the IS 456 Annex G-1 quadratic discriminant is negative, the slab is too thin for the applied moment with the chosen grades. The correct response is to throw (or set deflectionStatus=FAIL with a diagnostic). Returning 0 Ast causes all downstream checks to see a minimum-steel result, masking the failure.
deviations.decidedValue: throw SlabInputValidationError with message 'section under-sized: discriminant negative at Mu=X kNm'
deviations.notes: Fix is in W03. Do not patch silently.

deviations.sourceValue: golden regression must compare computed values to accepted reference values
deviations.codeValue: checks sheet count (46), sheet names, and two formula patterns only
deviations.description: verify-kherwara-excel-golden.ts is named 'golden' but performs zero numeric comparisons against known-good values. It only asserts structural properties (sheet count, sheet names, SUM formula patterns, HYDRAULICS cross-references). A calculation error in any cell would pass this check.
deviations.decidedValue: add at least 10 spot-checked cell values from the Kherwara reference workbook (SOM-KHW oracle) once W02A provides them
deviations.notes: Blocked on W02A providing GOLDEN-ORACLE.json values. The structural check is not wrong — it is incomplete.

deviations.sourceValue: git lfs pull must run before any test reads an .xlsx fixture
deviations.codeValue: FIXED: the test job's checkout sets lfs: true (.github/workflows/ci.yml). The docker-build job's checkout still omits it, which is correct — that job builds an image and reads no fixture.
deviations.description: .gitattributes LFS-tracks *.xlsx. CI's test-job checkout originally did not set lfs: true, so VARIABLE_SELECTION_SHEET.xlsx and docs/week-0/demo_bridge_raw.xlsx arrived as 130-byte Git LFS pointer files, and any script or test that read them got a pointer instead of a workbook.
deviations.decidedValue: lfs: true added to the test job's checkout step
deviations.notes: Closed, but not unguarded: the anchor below fails the gate if the fix is silently reverted.
